function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

We need to compute time for each leg using light travel time formula: time = distance / speed_of_light. But distance is given in light-years; we can convert to meters: 1 light-year = speed_of_light * seconds in one year. So distance in meters = distance_in_light_years * speed_of_light * seconds_per_year. Then time in seconds = distance_in_meters / speed_of_light = distance_in_light_years * seconds_per_year. So essentially time in seconds equals distance_in_light_years * seconds_per_year. So we can compute times directly: 4.22 ly -> 4.22 * seconds_per_year. 6.1 ly -> 6.1 * seconds_per_year. 5.88 ly -> 5.88 * seconds_per_year. Then sum them.
